title: Photon-nucleon entanglement in Compton scattering at low and high energies
abstract: We study spin-spin entanglement in the final state photon-nucleon system in Compton scattering, both at low energy below the pion threshold and at high energy in perturbative QCD to next-to-leading order. We first establish a no-go theorem showing that, for any spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ target, entanglement cannot be generated in unpolarized Compton scattering if the scattering amplitudes are real. We then consider polarized Compton scattering off the electron, the proton and the neutron. At low energy, we uncover a rich variety of maximally entangled Bell states and their unitary equivalents realized across different regions of the kinematic plane. Interestingly, the proton and neutron targets exhibit distinct patterns of entanglement. In the neutron case, the electric and magnetic polarizabilities dramatically influence the pattern and even the existence of entanglement. This suggests that entanglement can serve as a novel tool for investigating the detailed electromagnetic properties of the nucleons.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes spin-spin entanglement in Compton scattering, treating the outgoing photon and nucleon as a two-qubit system. It develops formalisms using helicity amplitudes to calculate the entanglement measure ($\lambda_{\min}$), demonstrating that polarization is crucial for generating entanglement. The findings suggest this quantum diagnostic tool can map out detailed electromagnetic structure of nucleons.
main_problem: The study investigates spin-spin entanglement generated in the final state photon-nucleon system during Compton scattering at both low and high energies.
main_result: The authors established a no-go theorem for unpolarized scattering with real amplitudes, but found that polarized scattering reveals rich patterns of maximally entangled Bell states, suggesting entanglement is a novel tool to probe nucleon electromagnetic properties.
method: The analysis involves calculating the two-qubit spin density matrix ($ho$) using helicity amplitudes derived from scattering cross-sections in different kinematic regimes (low/high energy).
model_or_system: The physical system is Compton scattering off a spin-1/2 nucleon (proton or neutron), treated as an outgoing photon and nucleon two-qubit quantum state.
key_observables: Spin density matrix ($ho$), minimum eigenvalue of the partially transposed density matrix ($\lambda_{\min}$), polarization vectors ($\vec{B}_N, \vec{B}_\gamma$), and correlation matrices ($C_{ab}$).
important_parameters: Photon energy ($\omega$) relative to pion mass ($m_\pi$); electric and magnetic polarizabilities ($\alpha_E,  eta_M$); scattering angle ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on working in the Center-of-Mass (CM) frame; specific approximations are used for high energy via perturbative QCD/GPDs.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates Compton scattering kinematics. Figure 2 shows contour plots of $\lambda_{\min}$ mapping entanglement strength across varying photon energy and scattering angle for electron-target scattering.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general formalism using helicity amplitudes to construct the density matrix, proving a no-go theorem in unpolarized cases, then detailing low-energy results sensitive to polarizabilities, and finally extending the framework to high-energy QCD calculations.
why_interesting: While focused on particle physics (QCD/Electromagnetism), the core methodology—quantifying entanglement via density matrices and partial transposition criteria ($\lambda_{\min}$)—is directly transferable to analyzing quantum correlations in complex many-body or open quantum systems studied in AMO physics.
